# Comprehensive Requirements Quality Checklist: Automated Demo Script

**Purpose**: Full-spectrum deep-dive validating requirement completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage across all domains (CLI, pipeline, CI, governance, seed data, multilingual)  
**Created**: 2025-07-18  
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)  
**Depth**: Thorough  
**Audience**: Author & Reviewer  

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 — Are all 7 pipeline phases explicitly defined with entry/exit criteria, or only named? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities — Pipeline Stage]
- [ ] CHK002 — Are agent startup order and inter-agent initialization dependencies specified, or is startup assumed to be independent? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 — Is the health check protocol defined (what constitutes a healthy agent, timeout, retry policy)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK004 — Are specific non-zero exit codes defined for different failure classes (health check failure, stage failure, seed data error, invalid arguments), or only "non-zero" generically? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK005 — Is the JSON output schema for the structured summary explicitly defined or only described narratively? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK006 — Are the exact fields and structure of the audit trail decision records formally specified (beyond narrative attributes in Key Entities)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011 / Key Entities — Decision Record]
- [ ] CHK007 — Are the Stage Handoff payload contents defined per agent-to-agent transition, or only generically as "data transferred"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012 / Key Entities — Stage Handoff]
- [ ] CHK008 — Is the "activation" phase fully specified — what health checks, startup sequencing, and readiness gates it includes? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications — 7 phases]
- [ ] CHK009 — Is the "audit summary" phase fully specified — what aggregation, metrics, and post-pipeline reporting it produces? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications — 7 phases]
- [ ] CHK010 — Are the contents and format of verbose-mode narration specified (log format, section headers, progress indicators), or only described as "human-readable"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK011 — Is the `--help` output or CLI usage documentation specified for the argparse interface? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK012 — Are error message formats and content requirements specified for CLI argument validation failures? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK013 — Is the simulated disaster signal structure fully defined (beyond the five attributes listed in Key Entities)? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities — Simulated Signal]
- [ ] CHK014 — Is the number of simulated signals to ingest specified, or only the minimum of "at least one"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK015 — Are the specific seed data files required from the data directory enumerated (file names, paths, expected schemas)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK016 — Are channel distribution targets for multilingual alerts specified beyond being mentioned in US2-AS3? [Completeness, Gap — US2 Acceptance Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK017 — Is the relationship between the demo script and the existing `create_app()` factory pattern documented as a formal interface dependency? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK019 — Is "healthy" quantified for agent health checks — what specific conditions constitute a passing health check? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]

- [ ] CHK023 — Is "confidence level" in cross-agent handoffs defined with a scale, range, or enumeration? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK024 — Is "safety-critical" formally defined — which specific decisions qualify, and what criteria classify a decision as safety-critical? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK025 — Is "above threshold" for resource allocation approval quantified with specific threshold values or a configuration mechanism? [Clarity, Spec §US3 Acceptance Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK026 — Is the "configured threshold" for policy escalation defined — where is it configured, what are defaults, and what format? [Clarity, Spec §US3 Acceptance Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK027 — Is "large-scale evacuation" defined with measurable criteria that distinguish it from a standard evacuation? [Clarity, Spec §US3 Acceptance Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK028 — Is "supporting data references" in decision records defined — are these file paths, IDs, URIs, or inline data? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK029 — Is "governance policy applied" in audit records defined — is this a policy name, policy version, policy ID, or free text? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK030 — Are "appropriate" outputs for different disaster scenarios defined — what makes cyclone outputs distinct from bushfire outputs? [Clarity, Spec §US4 Acceptance Scenario 2]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK035 — Is the FR-017 AIIMS workflow (activation → ingestion → analysis → recommendation → approval → alert publishing) consistent with the 7-phase model in FR-006 (activation, ingestion, risk analysis, evacuation routing, resource allocation, alert drafting, audit summary)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017 vs §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK036 — Does SC-002 (verbose < 5 min) align with US2-AS4 (< 5 min), and is the measurement method identical? [Consistency, Spec §SC-002 vs §US2]

- [ ] CHK052 — Are requirements defined for running the script with an unknown `--scenario` value (e.g., `--scenario earthquake`)? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK053 — Are requirements defined for the valid set of scenario values — is it an open or closed enumeration? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK054 — Are requirements defined for what stdout contains in non-verbose mode when `--output` is NOT specified (JSON only? progress indicators? nothing until completion?)? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-006/FR-008]
- [ ] CHK055 — Are requirements defined for running multiple concurrent instances of the demo script — is there any shared state or file locking concern? [Coverage, Gap]

## Scenario Coverage — Exception & Error Flows

- [ ] CHK056 — Are requirements defined for partial pipeline failure recovery — if agent 3 of 5 fails, what state are agents 1–2 left in? [Coverage, Exception — Spec §Edge Cases / Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK057 — Are requirements defined for agent health check timeout — how long does the script wait before declaring a health check failure? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK058 — Are requirements defined for distinguishing between a health check failure and a mid-pipeline agent failure in the exit code or output? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK059 — Are requirements defined for what happens when seed data validation fails for some but not all files — fail-fast on first invalid file or report all errors? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK060 — Are requirements defined for graceful shutdown signal handling beyond Ctrl+C (e.g., SIGTERM in CI containers)? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK061 — Are requirements defined for the behavior when the `data/` directory itself is missing or inaccessible? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK062 — Are requirements defined for what "orphaned processes" means in the Ctrl+C edge case — are agents spawned as subprocesses? (Conflicts with "in-process" from FR-002) [Coverage, Ambiguity — Spec §Edge Cases vs §FR-002]

## Notes

- This checklist tests the **quality of the requirements** in spec.md — not whether the implementation works.
- Each item asks whether something is clearly specified, consistently defined, or adequately covered.
- Items marked `[Gap]` indicate requirements that appear to be missing entirely.
- Items marked `[Ambiguity]` indicate language that could be interpreted multiple ways.
- Items marked `[Consistency]` flag potential conflicts between different spec sections.
- The existing `requirements.md` checklist covers high-level readiness; this checklist performs a deep-dive into specific requirement quality issues.
- **Key conflict to resolve**: CHK041/CHK098 — the fail-fast principle (Clarifications) directly contradicts the partial-completion edge case for missing language templates.
- **Key gap cluster**: CHK004/CHK005/CHK006/CHK007 — multiple output schemas are described narratively but not formally defined.
